'''Dame Eleanor Jane Milner-Gulland''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|DBE}} (born 3 June 1967) is the Tasso Leventis Professor of Biodiversity in the Department of Biology at the [[University of Oxford]], and director of the Interdisciplinary Centre for Conservation Science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-ej-milner-gulland |title=Professor EJ Milner Gulland |website=University of Oxford |language=en|access-date=2018-04-01}}</ref> She is an expert on understanding and influencing human behaviour to reduce biodiversity loss, on enabling businesses to improve their environmental and social sustainability, and on controlling the illegal wildlife trade. She is particularly known for her work on the ecology and conservation of the [[Saiga antelope|Saiga Antelope]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.marshchristiantrust.org/award/marsh-ecology-award/|title=Marsh Ecology Award|website=www.marshchristiantrust.org|access-date=2018-04-01}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Milner-Gulland was born on 3 June 1967 in [[Cuckfield]], Sussex.<ref name=":1">{{Cite encyclopedia |entry=Milner-Gulland, Prof. Eleanor Jane |encyclopedia=UK Who's Who |language=en|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.286964 |title=Milner-Gulland, Prof. Eleanor Jane, (Born 3 June 1967), Tasso Leventis Professor of Biodiversity, Department of Zoology, University of Oxford, since 2015; Fellow of Merton College, Oxford, since 2015 |date=2016 }}</ref> She is the elder daughter of the renowned Russian scholar [[Robin Milner-Gulland]] and the artist Alison Milner-Gulland.<ref name=":1" /> She completed her undergraduate education at [[New College, Oxford]] in Pure and Applied Biology. She then went to [[Imperial College London]] to complete a PhD in conservation biology supervised by [[John Beddington]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |degree=PhD |title=The exploitation of certain large mammals for trade: the implications for management |publisher=University of London |last=Milner-Gulland |first=Eleanor |date=October 1991 |hdl=10044/1/8376 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> Her thesis was entitled ''The exploitation of certain large mammals for trade: the implications for management'' which she submitted in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |last=J.|first=Milner-Gulland, E.|date=1991|title=The exploitation of certain large mammals for trade: the implications for management |website=British Library |url=https://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.282699}}</ref>

==Career==
After completing her PhD, Milner-Gulland became a junior research fellow at New College, Oxford. In 1994, she became a lecturer in mathematical ecology at the University of Warwick. In 1998, she moved back to Imperial College, where she stayed until 2015. In 2007, she was appointed Professor of Conservation Science. In 2015 she became the Tasso Leventis Professor of Biodiversity at the University of Oxford and a fellow of [[Merton College, Oxford|Merton College]]. In 2019 she became an official fellow of [[Parks College, Oxford|Parks College]] (later renamed [[Reuben College, Oxford|Reuben College]])<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/about/organisation/future-projects/parks-college/people |title=Parks College People |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=University of Oxford |access-date=2019-11-29 }}</ref> where she was Theme Lead for Environmental Change.<ref>{{cite web|date=22 September 2020|title=Prof E.J. Milner-Gulland & Prof Sir Charles Godfray in conversation: "Resetting our relationship with nature in a post-COVID world"|url=https://www.oxfordmartin.ox.ac.uk/events/nature-in-a-post-covid-world/|publisher=[[Oxford Martin School]], [[University of Oxford]]|location=UK|access-date=31 July 2021}}</ref> However, she moved back to Merton College in 2021.

Milner-Gulland is a conservation scientist whose work is at the interface of social and biological systems. She is the founder and chair of the Saiga Conservation Alliance<ref>{{Cite web|title=Professor EJ Milner-Gulland |url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/news-and-events/find-an-expert/professor-ej-milner-gulland|access-date=2018-04-01|website=University of Oxford|language=en}}</ref> and has launched a number of initiatives which aim to change the real-world conversation around conservation, including the Conservation Hierarchy approach to meeting a global vision of restoring nature, the Conservation Optimism movement and the Alliance of Nature Positive Universities. She is the Chair of the UK Government's Darwin Expert Committee and a Trustee of the UK [[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=WWF Trustees|url=https://www.wwf.org.uk/trustees|access-date=2018-04-01|website=WWF|language=en}}</ref> In 2015, Milner-Gulland became a Pew Fellow of Marine Conservation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pewtrusts.org/en/projects/marine-fellows/fellows-directory/2015/ej-milner-gulland-phd|title=E.J. Milner-Gulland, Ph.D.|website=www.pewtrusts.org|access-date=2018-04-01}}</ref> She is also a trustee of the [[Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wildlife.durrell.org/about/the-people/board-of-trustees/eleanor-jane-milner-gulland/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180414172125/http://wildlife.durrell.org/about/the-people/board-of-trustees/eleanor-jane-milner-gulland/ |archive-date=2018-04-14 |title=Eleanor Jane Milner-Gulland |website=Durrell Wildlife Conservation Trust |language=en|access-date=2018-04-01}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Milner-Gulland was appointed [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE) in the [[2023 Birthday Honours]] for services to international conservation.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=64082|supp=y|page=B8|date=17 June 2023}}</ref>

* [[Marsh Award for Conservation Biology]] (2001)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Marsh Award for Conservation Biology|url=http://www.marshchristiantrust.org/award/marsh-award-for-conservation-biology/|access-date=2018-04-01|website=www.marshchristiantrust.org}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
* [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]] (2008)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/eleanor-milner-gulland-7682/|title=Eleanor Milner-Gulland|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-04-01}}</ref>
* Society for Conservation Biology Distinguished Service Award (2019)
